text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A $2 million grant by Canadian government to Nigerian opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) is tearing the group apart over how to spend the money.
- Nigeria's crude oil reserves to last 21 years, says department of petroleum resources.
- Nigerian oil refinery output rises to 75 percent of installed capacity, says director of petroleum resources Wilson Dublin-Green.
- Foreign exchange demand by banks at weekly auction rose by $2.54 million last week, says Central Bank.
- Lagos state doctors suspend week-old strike.
- Nigerian Boeing 727 plane which crashed on November 7 killing all 142 people on board was fit to fly, according to its aviation records.
- Security officials meet to review state of the nation following car bomb attack last week which killed three persons.
- British Airways willing to help troubled Nigerian national carrier utilise some of its unused routes, its international relations manager David Richardson tells Nigerian journalists in London.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani says government is considering shelving the idea of taking golden shares in the four biggest banks in the country.
- Nigeria denies visas to four Canadian officials for the visit of Commonwealth group to Abuja with official sources accusing the four of being spies
